\looseness=-2 We presented ACR-VLA, an adaptive inference-time correction pipeline for frozen flow-matching VLAs. A $K{=}2$ pairwise $L_2$ uncertainty probe ($\rho{=}0.9979$) gates a lightweight CRM (${\sim}$327K parameters). On SmolVLA (0.4B) across four LIBERO suites, unconditional CRM correction is unstable ($-$2.2\,pp Long, $-$1.2\,pp Object, $+$1.1\,pp Spatial), while ACR-VLA's adaptive gate provides improvement where the VLA is uncertain ($+$1.3--2.1\,pp on Spatial and Goal) and preserves baseline where it is confident (Object $+$0.1\,pp, Long $-$0.3\,pp within noise). The key finding is that adaptive gating, not correction strength, is the mechanism: the gate correctly allocates correction to uncertain steps while protecting confident ones.
\textbf{Limitations.}\enspace Effect sizes are $+$1.3--2.1\,pp on high-uncertainty suites (Spatial and Goal, 3 seeds each). On low-uncertainty suites, ACR-VLA preserves baseline: Object $+$0.1\,pp (5 seeds), Long $-$0.3\,pp${=}0.2\sigma$ (3 seeds). The pairwise $L_2$ uncertainty probe measures sample disagreement, not correctness; on Long (trigger rate ${\sim}$4\%), the VLA may produce confident but incorrect outputs that escape gating detection. Future work could combine disagreement-based and prediction-error-based uncertainty signals. The CRM requires task-specific calibration data and stochastic sample diversity; deterministic VLAs produce near-identical samples and lie outside scope (Appendix~\ref{sec:applicability}). Broader cross-VLA generalization and real-robot transfer remain future work. AI tools assisted with code and manuscript.

\looseness=-2 We presented ACR-VLA, an adaptive inference-time correction pipeline for frozen flow-matching VLAs. A $K{=}2$ pairwise $L_2$ uncertainty probe ($\rho{=}0.9979$) gates a lightweight CRM (${\sim}$327K parameters). On SmolVLA (0.4B) across four LIBERO suites, unconditional CRM correction is unstable ($-$2.2\,pp Long, $-$1.2\,pp Object, $+$1.1\,pp Spatial), while ACR-VLA's adaptive gate provides improvement where the VLA is uncertain ($+$1.3--2.1\,pp on Spatial and Goal) and preserves baseline where it is confident (Object $+$0.1\,pp, Long $-$0.3\,pp within noise). The key finding is that adaptive gating, not correction strength, is the mechanism: the gate correctly allocates correction to uncertain steps while protecting confident ones.

\section{Limitations}
\label{sec:limitations}

\looseness=-1 \textbf{Effect sizes and statistical power.}\enspace Improvements are $+$1.3--2.1\,pp on high-uncertainty suites (Spatial and Goal, 3 seeds each). On low-uncertainty suites, ACR-VLA preserves baseline: Object $+$0.1\,pp (5 seeds), Long $-$0.3\,pp${=}0.2\sigma$ (3 seeds). With $n \leq 5$ seeds per condition, we report directional consistency rather than statistical significance.

\looseness=-1 \textbf{Confidently wrong steps.}\enspace The pairwise $L_2$ uncertainty probe measures sample disagreement, not correctness. On Long (trigger rate ${\sim}$4\%), the VLA may produce confident but systematically incorrect outputs that escape gating detection. Future work could combine disagreement-based and prediction-error-based uncertainty signals to address this failure mode.

\looseness=-1 \textbf{Scope and generalization.}\enspace The CRM requires task-specific calibration data (10 demonstrations per task) and stochastic sample diversity; deterministic VLAs produce near-identical samples and lie outside scope (Appendix~\ref{sec:applicability}). All experiments use LIBERO simulation; real-robot transfer, where action noise and latency constraints differ, remains future work. Cross-VLA generalization beyond SmolVLA is preliminary (Section~\ref{sec:cross_vla}).

AI tools assisted with code and manuscript.

1	\section{Related Work}\label{sec:related_work}
2	
3	\looseness=-1 \paragraph{VLA robustness.} Vision-language-action models have progressed from tokenized prediction~\cite{brohan2023rt2,kim2024openvla,ghosh2024octo} to generative approaches based on diffusion~\cite{chi2023diffusion_policy} and flow matching~\cite{black2024pi0,shukor2025smolvla}. Robustness evaluations~\cite{fei2025liberoplus} show that current VLAs lose over 65\,pp under deployment perturbations. Training-time defenses (SRPO~\cite{srpo2025}, RobustVLA~\cite{robustvla2025}, DiG-Flow~\cite{digflow2025}, TT-VLA~\cite{liu2026ttvla}) improve robustness but require retraining or reward engineering.
4	
5	\looseness=-1 \paragraph{Inference-time correction.} Among frozen-VLA methods, ReconVLA~\cite{chen2026reconvla} provides uncertainty quantification but no learned correction; SC-VLA~\cite{liu2026scvla} requires task-level RL; VLA-Pilot~\cite{li2025vlapilot} uses evolutionary optimization at 2.41\,s per step. A2C2~\cite{a2c2_2025} is the closest concurrent work: it learns a correction head addressing \emph{temporal staleness} within action chunks. Our pipeline targets a complementary problem, namely \emph{initial action quality}, with multi-sample centering, explicit magnitude control, and adaptive per-step compute allocation. ACR-VLA draws only $K{=}2$ samples in a single batched forward pass and uses their pairwise $L_2$ distance as a per-step uncertainty probe.
